description: 20 labeled disputes with human ground-truth verdicts (claimant share %). Used to benchmark verdict accuracy.

cases.summary: Freelancer took deposit but delivered nothing
cases.description: Client paid 0.5 STT for a landing page. Freelancer disappeared after 2 weeks. GitHub repo is empty. No demo URL. No communication for 10 days.
cases.claimantStatement: I paid the full bond up front. Bob delivered nothing - no commits, no demo, no Figma. He stopped responding 10 days ago.
cases.respondentStatement: I had a family emergency. I will deliver next week.

cases.summary: Freelancer delivered Figma only, no implementation
cases.description: Client paid 1.0 STT for a landing page implementation. Freelancer delivered only a Figma design, no code, no deployment.
cases.claimantStatement: Agreed scope was a deployed landing page. I received only a Figma file. The contract is in IPFS. No code was written.
cases.respondentStatement: Design phase took longer than expected because the brief kept changing. Implementation was milestone 2 and the client never approved milestone 1.

cases.summary: Delivered on time but quality is poor
cases.description: Freelancer delivered a working website on the deadline, but mobile layout is broken and 3 buttons don't work.
cases.claimantStatement: The site is broken on mobile and 3 CTA buttons do nothing. I cannot launch this.
cases.respondentStatement: I delivered on time. Bugs can be fixed in maintenance. The spec didn't mention mobile testing.

cases.summary: Freelancer delivered exactly what was agreed, on time
cases.description: Freelancer delivered all milestones on time. Client now claims he never wanted the project and wants a refund.
cases.claimantStatement: I changed my mind and want a refund.
cases.respondentStatement: All milestones signed off via Slack. Live deployment URL provided. Code in client's GitHub org.

cases.summary: Client kept adding features beyond agreed scope
cases.description: Original scope was 5 pages. Client added 4 more pages mid-project without renegotiating price. Freelancer delivered the original 5 but refused the extras.
cases.claimantStatement: Freelancer only delivered 5 out of 9 pages I needed.
cases.respondentStatement: Contract was for 5 pages. I delivered 5. The other 4 were never part of the scope and were never paid for.

cases.summary: SaaS provider missed 99.9% uptime SLA badly
cases.description: Annual SaaS contract guaranteed 99.9% uptime. Actual uptime over the quarter was 92% with three multi-hour outages affecting paying users.
cases.claimantStatement: Contract guarantees 99.9% uptime with refund clause. Status page shows 92% this quarter.
cases.respondentStatement: The outages were due to AWS regional failures outside our control. Force majeure applies.

cases.summary: SaaS had brief degradation, mostly within SLA
cases.description: Hosting service had a 45-minute outage in one quarter. Otherwise uptime is 99.95%, above the contracted 99.9%.
cases.claimantStatement: There was a 45-minute outage that disrupted my business call. I want a partial refund.
cases.respondentStatement: Quarterly uptime was 99.93%, above the contracted 99.9%. SLA was met.

cases.summary: NFT project never delivered promised utility
cases.description: User minted NFT for 0.1 ETH equivalent based on roadmap promising metaverse access. 6 months later, no metaverse, no Discord activity, team anonymous.
cases.claimantStatement: Roadmap promised metaverse access by Q2. Q2 is over. Discord is dead. Devs are anonymous and stopped posting.
cases.respondentStatement: Markets are tough. We are still building. Plans have shifted.

cases.summary: NFT delivered exactly as the mint page promised
cases.description: User minted a pure-art NFT collection. The mint page only promised the JPEG, nothing else. User now demands a refund because secondary market dropped.
cases.claimantStatement: The floor price collapsed and the artist has not been posting much.
cases.respondentStatement: The mint page promised only the artwork and a low-res reveal. I delivered both. There was no utility roadmap.

cases.summary: Buyer received a counterfeit item
cases.description: Buyer paid for a 'authentic' Rolex on a P2P marketplace. Receiver inspected it - movement is generic Chinese clone. Seller listed it as 'authentic, with papers'.
cases.claimantStatement: Watch arrived. Authentication shop confirmed it's a counterfeit. Listing said 'authentic with papers'. No papers were included.
cases.respondentStatement: I sold it as-is. Buyer should have inspected before purchase.

cases.summary: Buyer changed mind after receiving item exactly as described
cases.description: Buyer purchased a used laptop. It arrived matching the listing photos exactly. Buyer now says they 'don't like the color'.
cases.claimantStatement: I don't like the color anymore.
cases.respondentStatement: Item matches the listing. Photos show the exact color. Buyer never asked questions before purchase.

cases.summary: Item arrived damaged due to seller's poor packaging
cases.description: Buyer purchased a fragile vintage camera. Seller wrapped it in newspaper only. Camera arrived with broken lens mount.
cases.claimantStatement: Camera lens mount is cracked. Seller used newspaper only. Carrier confirms packaging was inadequate.
cases.respondentStatement: Carrier damaged it during transit. I am not liable for shipping damage.

cases.summary: Tenant caused damage beyond normal wear
cases.description: Tenant moved out leaving stained carpet, hole in wall, and broken appliance. Landlord bond was held in escrow.
cases.claimantStatement: Landlord is refusing to return my bond over minor wear.
cases.respondentStatement: Carpet professionally cleaned showed permanent stains. Drywall has a 6-inch punch hole. Microwave does not power on. Move-in inspection signed by tenant.

cases.summary: Landlord withheld bond for normal wear and tear
cases.description: Tenant moved out after 2 years. Light scuffs on walls, slightly worn carpet. Landlord withheld full bond claiming damage.
cases.claimantStatement: I lived there 2 years. Scuffs are normal wear. Landlord wants to repaint and charge me.
cases.respondentStatement: Walls have many scuffs. Repainting cost is real.

cases.summary: Consultant delivered report 3 weeks late, with caveats
cases.description: Consultant was due to deliver market research by date X. Delivered 3 weeks late. Report quality is solid but client missed an investor meeting.
cases.claimantStatement: Report was 3 weeks late, I missed the investor pitch I commissioned it for.
cases.respondentStatement: Client kept adding interview targets which extended the timeline. Final report is comprehensive.

cases.summary: Consultant invoiced but never delivered
cases.description: Consultant invoiced for 40 hours of strategy work over 2 months. No deck, no notes, no calls recorded.
cases.claimantStatement: I have no deliverables. No meeting notes. No deck. The consultant only had 2 calls with me.
cases.respondentStatement: Strategy work is intangible. I delivered value through conversations.

cases.summary: Validator was slashed for double-signing
cases.description: Delegator's stake was slashed because the validator double-signed. Validator claims it was a software bug.
cases.claimantStatement: I lost 8% of my stake because the validator double-signed. They should compensate me from their commission earnings.
cases.respondentStatement: It was a software bug in the new version, not malice. Slashing should not pass through to delegators.

cases.summary: DAO grantee took funds but produced no output
cases.description: DAO grant of 5000 STT for an analytics dashboard. 6 months later: no repo, no demo, no progress reports.
cases.claimantStatement: Grantee has not posted any updates, has not opened any commits, has not delivered the dashboard.
cases.respondentStatement: Building takes time. I am still working on it privately.

cases.summary: DAO grantee delivered alpha but missed deadline
cases.description: DAO grant of 3000 STT for a wallet integration. Grantee delivered a working alpha at 80% spec, but 2 months late.
cases.claimantStatement: Delivery was 2 months late and the alpha is missing 20% of the agreed features.
cases.respondentStatement: Alpha is live and working. The missing 20% is in code review. I have shipped 80% of the spec.

cases.summary: Both parties at fault due to ambiguous contract
cases.description: Two parties disagree on what 'production-ready' means. Original contract did not define the term. Freelancer's deliverable works but lacks tests and CI.
cases.claimantStatement: Production-ready means CI, tests, monitoring. None of those exist.
cases.respondentStatement: Production-ready means it runs in production without crashing. The site is live and serves users.
